title: Construction Slip and Extension Days on the Builder Extended Rate Lock
content:
When the home's completion has slipped, extra days are counted when a Builder Extended Rate Lock is extended.

**Rule.** The construction slip is the calendar days from the Home Purchase Agreement's contract completion date to its estimated completion date. A slip above 30 days adds one day for every 14 days of slip, any part counted as a whole; a slip of one day up to 30 days adds 2 days; no slip adds none. The days are added to the days to cover before they are rounded up to whole increments.

## Method by slip

| Construction slip | Days added to the days to cover |
|---|---|
| none (estimated completion on or before the contract completion date) | none |
| 1 to 30 days | a flat 2 days |
| above 30 days | the slip divided by 14, any part of 14 counted as a whole day |

## Boundary and worked cases (hypothetical slips)

| Slip | Days added |
|---|---|
| 0 | 0 |
| 1 | 2 |
| 30 | 2 |
| 31 | 3 (31 divided by 14 is 2 and a part, counted as 3) |
| 42 | 3 |
| 43 | 4 |
| 70 | 5 |

Both dates are read from the Home Purchase Agreement record of the agreement the lock finances.
